decisions.text: Claude Code skills and workflows reach a user repo as pointers: init writes symlinks .claude/skills/<name> and .claude/workflows/<name>.js into the installed package (node_modules/cookwright), the same mechanism Codex needs (.agents/skills/ pointers). The 2026-10-15 decision 'Claude Code users receive skills through the plugin' is superseded. Precondition before bundle init: one Claude Code session in a scratch repo measures a skill pointer into node_modules listing the skill, the same pointer dangling neither listing it nor breaking the session, and one named workflow run through a .claude/workflows/<name>.js pointer into node_modules running to its return value, since the bundle runner depends on that route.
The setup skill is named setup, as E-012 names it; a user's own skill of that name shadows it with a WARN; a later rename costs one updated row per user.

scripts/ci/fixture.sh pins create-expo-app to an exact version as one constant, prints it on the script's first output line, and the version is bumped deliberately: a harness CI that goes red on an upstream scaffold release is property-3 rot.

The README's Releases section carries the exact release order and §8's developer's-hands list follows it: npm version X.Y.Z --no-git-tag-version, commit; git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m 'released: YYYY-MM-DD' plus note: lines; npx cookwright changelog, commit; git push --follow-tags (pre-push runs the gate and the changelog check); npm publish. The first release after this bundle is 0.1.0.
